answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable token for a fixed period before it can claim work or vote. The protocol caps influence by locked stake, not by account count, so splitting funds across a thousand identities grants no extra weight. A participant who tries to forge identities must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying market cost and losing liquidity; if caught violating rules, it can lose the stake. A pigment or jade label might decorate an account, but neither substitutes for collateral.
